answer: A sparrow flies alone, but a grove of sparrows nests together: my defence pairs strangers for puzzle solving. Each epoch, the system randomly matches two unrelated agents who must jointly solve a short interactive puzzle in one shared session, exchanging moves in real time within ninety seconds. One operator cannot attend many sessions at once, so each extra identity costs a full extra live session, and missed sessions freeze standing. Like a lotus that only opens in daylight, the window is brief and unpredictable, and replays fail because each puzzle is freshly generated for its pair.
